events.title: Thomas Cromwell is beheaded on Tower Hill
events.description: Henry VIII's chief minister, architect of the break with Rome and the Dissolution of the Monasteries, was executed for treason and heresy. His fall followed the king's disastrous marriage to Anne of Cleves.
events.html: Henry VIII's chief minister, architect of the break with Rome and the Dissolution of the Monasteries, was executed for treason and heresy. His fall followed the king's disastrous marriage to Anne of Cleves.

events.title: Johann Sebastian Bach dies in Leipzig
events.description: Bach died aged 65 after failed eye operations. Little valued by his immediate successors, his music was revived in the nineteenth century, and he is now ranked among the greatest composers.
events.html: Bach died aged 65 after failed eye operations. Little valued by his immediate successors, his music was revived in the nineteenth century, and he is now ranked among the greatest composers.

events.title: The 14th Amendment is certified as part of the US Constitution
events.description: Secretary of State William Seward certified the 14th Amendment, guaranteeing citizenship and equal protection of the laws. It became the basis for many landmark civil rights rulings.
events.html: Secretary of State William Seward certified the 14th Amendment, guaranteeing citizenship and equal protection of the laws. It became the basis for many landmark civil rights rulings.

events.title: Austria-Hungary declares war on Serbia
events.description: One month after the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand, Austria-Hungary declared war on Serbia. Within a week Russia, Germany, France and Britain were drawn in, and the First World War had begun.
events.html: One month after the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand, Austria-Hungary declared war on Serbia. Within a week Russia, Germany, France and Britain were drawn in, and the First World War had begun.

events.title: US troops drive the Bonus Army out of Washington
events.description: On Hoover's orders, troops under Douglas MacArthur used tear gas and bayonets to clear camps of First World War veterans demanding early payment of bonuses. The scenes damaged Hoover's re-election hopes.
